q1: Decision: if chemotherapy starts before the ctDNA result is back, I would start single-agent oral temozolomide, 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of a 28-day cycle, after baseline CBC, liver function and creatinine. I would not start an anthracycline-based regimen for this unclassified tumour. Options considered: (a) Temozolomide alone: oral, crosses the blood-brain barrier, low toxicity, and the agent I would use as a bridge while the diagnosis is open. Activity in sarcoma-like tumours is modest, so this is a bridge, not a definitive treatment. (b) Lomustine: CNS-penetrant nitrosourea with more myelosuppression; reserve it for progression on temozolomide. (c) Doxorubicin-based regimens (doxorubicin with dacarbazine, or with ifosfamide): the standard for high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma, but doxorubicin penetrates the brain poorly, carries cardiotoxicity (baseline echocardiogram needed), and should be chosen only once the entity is supported. (d) Entity-specific regimens (for example Ewing-type or melanoma-directed therapy) are not appropriate until those diagnoses are supported. Reasons: the residual tumour is growing after 60 Gy to the resection bed, and ECOG is 1, so there is a real case to act. Temozolomide carries the least risk and gives the best CNS delivery. The choice is documented as empirical, and the molecular result is expected to redirect therapy. Add MGMT promoter methylation to the methylation request on archival tissue, since it informs temozolomide response.
q2: Decision: no, I would not add a second chemotherapy drug now. I would continue single-agent temozolomide and reassess. Reasons: (1) The entity is unknown, so there is no evidence base for a specific combination, and a second cytotoxic agent adds myelosuppression and toxicity without a defined target. (2) Temozolomide has run for only several weeks, which is too short to judge response or progression. Reassess with contrast MRI at about 8 weeks from start (RANO criteria), or sooner for any clinical change. (3) The patient tolerates temozolomide well, so there is no toxicity reason to escalate. (4) The molecular result is due now and could replace chemotherapy with a targeted agent (see q3); a second cytotoxic drug would be the wrong step before then. If progression on temozolomide is confirmed and the molecular result gives no usable target, the next step would be lomustine added to temozolomide, with weekly blood counts for the first cycle. A doxorubicin-based regimen would be considered only if the tumour is confirmed as a sarcoma. Bevacizumab could be considered as a non-cytotoxic partner if perfusion MRI shows a hypervascular tumour.
q3: Decision: no. I would not stop chemotherapy or switch to targeted therapy on this report alone. I would continue temozolomide while confirming the alterations and looking for their origin. The full NGS report is not in the FHIR update, which contains only the 2026-12-15 request; I am taking the four alterations as stated in the question. Reasons: (1) The report is a lead, not a diagnosis. Plasma cell-free DNA from a brain lesion often carries a small tumour fraction, so the tumour fraction and variant allele frequencies must be checked. Clonal haematopoiesis and germline variants also appear in blood, so matched white-cell sequencing is needed, especially for STK11 and KRAS. (2) The FGFR2 fusion must be confirmed by RNA-based sequencing on tissue, because DNA-based fusion calls can be false positives. (3) The pattern does not fit a STAT6-negative CNS mesenchymal tumour. FGFR2 fusions, KRAS with STK11, and CTNNB1 are more typical of epithelial tumours (biliary, lung, liver). A high-grade spindle-cell carcinoma, or a metastasis from an epithelial primary, must therefore be excluded. Cytokeratin and carcinoma-lineage immunohistochemistry on the existing 2026-10-19 biopsy and 2026-10-28 resection blocks, plus CT chest, abdomen and pelvis or PET-CT, is the most important next step. If cytokeratin is positive, the whole plan changes. (4) Even if confirmed, each alteration has a different drug position. An FGFR2 fusion has approved FGFR inhibitors in cholangiocarcinoma, but intracranial activity is uncertain. KRAS needs the exact variant: G12C has sotorasib or adagrasib options, approved in lung and colorectal disease and otherwise by trial or off-label use. STK11 and CTNNB1 have no approved targeted agent. Plan: obtain the full report with variant details; confirm the fusion by RNA and the other variants on tissue; send matched normal sequencing; run cytokeratin immunohistochemistry; complete staging; and review at molecular tumour board. I would switch to a targeted agent only when a confirmed alteration matches a validated drug for a tumour type that pathology and staging support, ideally within a trial. Until then temozolomide continues, with reassessment on MRI.
